INTRODUCTIONM
In this lesson, you will learn about AC motor characteristics.
AC motors are very popular in industry because AC power is readily available.
AC motors are used when low starting currents are more important than speed control.
The AC induction motor is the most commonly used motor when low starting current is a characteristic.

DISCUSSION
Recall, AC motors are constructed from pole pairs and a rotor.
Two powers, each of a different phase are applied to the stator poles.
This sets up a rotating magnetic field around the rotor which produces motor action.

Rotor rotation or shaft speed, is never as great as synchronous speed.
The rotor is always trying to catch up or synchronize with the stator field speed.
Slip Speed = Synchronous Speed - Shaft Speed
The difference between synchronous speed and shaft speed is called slip speed or slip RPM.
Slip speed is how much the shaft speed lags behind the stator field speed.

Let's look at the relationship between the following AC induction motor characteristics: motor RPM, stator current and torque.
An AC motor has a unique relationship when comparing load to the following: motor RPM, stator current and torque.
Notice that as the load on the motor increases toward the rated load, stator current and torque increase.
At the rated load, RPM drops to between 85 and 95% of the synchronous speed.
The point where torque and RPM cross is the rated load RPM stated on many AC motors.
Increasing the load beyond the motor's rating will increase torque to maximum, while RPM remains relatively steady.
Unlike a DC motor, an AC motor has a peak torque that is not at maximum load (locked rotor).f
As the load is increased further, motor torque decreases.
This causes a rapid drop in RPM until the rotor is locked.
Low torque when the load is maximum increases the motor starting current. This is a prime reason for using AC induction motors.

Both torque and stator current increase as the motor load increases.
AC induction motors are typically classified as one phase, two phase or three phase machines.
The classification is determined by the number of input power phases required to operate the motor.
